person.note:
Godwin records his death and there are two entries to Jas Heath, one in 1828 and one in 1831. There are other Heaths in the diary, and Godwin refers to plain 'Heath'. We initially coded only those with Jas, but it seems likely that the family of engravers was well known to Godwin and that the late entries where he adds Jas may be to separate members of the same family, perhaps especially Charles Heath (1785-1848), Heath's son by Mary Phillipson. It should be noted that Godwin includes Heath in the 1796 list for 1788, and that Heath did become a major figure in the engraving and print world with a Royal Appointment in 1794, and associate membership to the Royal Academy in 1791. See ODNB for Heath family.
It may seem odd that Heath should feature prominently in the months immediately after Wollstonecraft's death, but itseems clear that Godwin aranged for Heath to engrave a portrait of her from the painting by Opie.
